key_insight: Photovoltaics look energetically strong at the panel level, but their net energy advantage shrinks sharply once grid reliability and firming are included.
engineering_relevance: For power-system design, the main challenge is not just generating low-carbon electricity, but delivering it continuously with enough net-energy surplus to support storage, backup, and grid infrastructure.
method: Includes component turnover, grids, storage, renewable overbuild, dispatchable backup, and fuel supply
Compares unfirmed renewable supply with battery, hydrogen, and gas-firmed delivery
evidence_signal: The abstract reports EROI and GWP100 ranges across firming options, showing large drops in EROI and large rises in emissions when moving from unfirmed PV/wind to reliable electricity supply.
watch_item: This is an accounting benchmark rather than a simulation or real-system prediction, and the illustrative favorable assumptions likely overstate performance versus actual deployment.
paper_title: Photovoltaics beyond the panel: system-level net energy under grid and firming constraints
